clue.text: Watches a women's diversion for infants

parts.note: to see is to watch
taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for women, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on a pastime put on by women for small children.
explanation.definitionFit: A see-saw is a playground plank that young children ride up and down for fun.

clue.text: Dairy product invented, is it suggested?

indicators.note: the question hints that the word for invented is not taken straight but read the other way round

parts.note: something invented has been made

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a dairy food was dreamt up by its makers.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: the question mark admits that MADE turned around to EDAM is only hinted at.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild round Dutch cheese, and cheese is made from milk on the farm.

clue.text: Reuse plug after replacing big sticker

indicators.note: replacing things puts them in new positions, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to fit an old plug again once something large and adhesive has been changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is an extremely strong adhesive, so it sticks things in a big way; a sticker is anything that adheres.

clue.text: Fantasy question about one woman's address

indicators.note: about means around, so the question word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: why is a question
I is the Roman numeral one
Ms is a title used to address a woman

explanation.surface: A fanciful enquiry concerning a single woman's home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests where she lives, but it is the form of address, the title Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playfully fanciful humour, the stuff of flights of imagination and fancy.

clue.text: Make a joke of the day I get promoted

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
taken as written
to rise is to go up in rank

explanation.surface: Someone laughs off the day they finally win promotion at work.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise is to ridicule something by mocking exaggeration, turning it into a laughing matter.

clue.text: Shocked as insolent aside is given the tabloid treatment

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted and thrown into disorder, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark caused offence and ended up splashed across the popular press.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabloid newspapers are known for lurid, exaggerated stories, which is exactly what a sensationalised report is.

clue.text: Draw apart and flop down, having a bit of a cry

parts.note: to tear is to pull apart
to drop is to fall or flop down

explanation.surface: Someone separates things, slumps down and sheds a few tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying consists of tears, and a single drop of one is a small part of the weeping.

clue.text: Arrive at a stretch of water

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to get to a place
second meaning: a straight length of river between bends

explanation.surface: A traveller comes to a long expanse of river.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for getting somewhere and a noun for a section of river.

clue.text: Disciple Mark entering the holy city, safe

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the mark goes within the city's name

parts.note: Sion is a variant spelling of Zion, the holy city of Jerusalem
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: One of the gospel writers arrives safely in Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like the evangelist, but it is just the letter M; a safe-breaker is a peterman in old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter is the full gospel name of the apostle Peter, one of Jesus's twelve disciples.

clue.text: Political group I nag to work out plan of action

parts.note: a camp is a faction holding a shared position

indicators.note: working something out involves shuffling it around, so the short phrase's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A member of a political faction keeps pestering colleagues to devise a strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised course of activity aimed at a goal, such as an election drive.

clue.text: Almost all weaponry is terrifying

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Nearly every weapon stockpiled is a frightening sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to frighten them, so the verb with -s matches the third-person phrase.

clue.text: Call bootblack out of bed to start work?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cheery phrase used to wake someone up

definitions.text: bootblack out of bed to start work?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a shoe-polisher gets up and begins polishing

explanation.surface: Someone wakes the shoeshine boy so he can begin his working day.
explanation.walkthrough: A bootblack polishes shoes, so for him getting up and shining is literally the job; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a traditional morning wake-up call telling a sleeper to get up and look lively.

clue.text: But one's decision should be anything but capricious

definitions.text: But one's decision should be anything but capricious

parts.words: But one's decision should be anything but capricious
parts.note: surface reading: a reproach that somebody's choice ought not to be whimsical
setter's reading: capricious means arbitrary, so this person's name sounds like that word but their judgement must be fair

explanation.surface: A complaint that a certain person's ruling should not be made on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the job title looks built from the word arbitrary, yet the role demands the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appointed to settle disputes must judge impartially on the evidence, never by whim.

clue.text: Defaced wall painting of mountain range

indicators.note: defaced suggests losing its face, the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a mural is a picture painted on a wall

explanation.surface: Vandals have spoiled a mural depicting some mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Urals are the range running north to south through Russia, dividing Europe from Asia.

clue.text: One recently dead put into the ground alone

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so the word for dead goes within the word for ground

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground's surface
the late someone is a person who has recently died

explanation.surface: A newly deceased person is buried by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being isolated means being cut off and solitary, with no one else around.

clue.text: Sweet, having skill to support small program

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting part sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: an applet is a small computer application
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A cute piece of software that is clever enough to help a little application.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a sweet is a dessert, and a fruit pie with pastry is a classic pudding.

clue.text: Not legitimate, so I usurp violently

indicators.note: doing something violently throws things about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pretender admits seizing power by force, without any lawful claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, lacking any valid basis or authority.

clue.text: Penalises wordplay that is too subtle

parts.note: to fine is to punish with a money penalty
a pun is a form of wordplay

explanation.surface: A setter is punished for clues whose cleverness goes over everyone's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Finespun describes argument or detail spun so finely that it becomes overly delicate or abstruse.

clue.text: Urgent request that may be bargained in America

definitions.text: that may be bargained in America
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a defendant's answer to a charge

explanation.surface: An insistent appeal that could be haggled over in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Plea bargaining, where a defendant admits a lesser charge in exchange for leniency, is a famous feature of American courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heartfelt appeal and a formal statement of guilty or not guilty in court.

clue.text: Footballers given a large handbook

parts.note: Man U is the nickname of Manchester United football club
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A football team is handed a big book of instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is an English Premier League club, commonly shortened to Man U.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual is a book of instructions or reference, the same thing as a handbook.

clue.text: This informs the media how to get out of seatbelt?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an official statement issued to journalists

definitions.text: how to get out of seatbelt?
definitions.note: an instruction phrase for a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: push the button that frees the buckle

explanation.surface: A puzzled passenger asks how to unbuckle, while someone issues news to journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two instructions, the phrase tells you to push the catch, then free yourself; the question mark marks the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisations issue a press release, a written announcement, so newspapers and broadcasters can report it.

clue.text: Run through film showing a half of rugby

definitions.note: scrum is the first half of the position name scrum-half

indicators.note: running through something means passing inside it, so the letter sits within the word for film

parts.note: scum is a film of dirt on a liquid's surface
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone plays back a movie featuring one half of a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' wants to be a movie; it is the thin layer on a pond. The scrum-half is a rugby position, so the answer is literally half of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum is the set piece where forwards bind together, and it forms one half of the name scrum-half.

clue.text: Aquatic creature and its habitat, loch?

parts.note: the creature lives in the sea
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A water animal wonders if its home is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals are marine mammals that hunt fish in the water and haul out on rocks.

clue.text: In store playing English hi-fi equipment

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the rearranged word
playing about with something rearranges it, so the shop word gets mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A shop has English music playing on its sound system.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereo is a sound system with two speaker channels, standard home audio gear.

clue.text: Wise guys touring Oz or the States for simple food

indicators.note: touring means going all around a place, so the wise men surround the country

parts.note: sages are wise men
AUS abbreviates Australia, nicknamed Oz, and its last two letters are US, the States

explanation.surface: Clever men travel round Australia or America in search of plain meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is the informal name for Australia; the wording lets the abbreviation be read as either country's.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages are basic everyday fare, as in sausage and mash or a hot dog.

clue.text: Set to receive such ideal land

definitions.meaning: first meaning: assured of getting something

definitions.note: describes a land, so the answer is the adjective before it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... Land, an ideal place of fulfilment

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be handed a perfect plot of property.
explanation.definitionFit: Being promised something means it is pledged to you; the Promised Land is the Biblical paradise of Canaan.

clue.text: Attack poor service and hurry away

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed
to fly is to rush off

explanation.surface: Someone criticises bad customer service and then storms out.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is an idiom for launching a sudden verbal or physical assault on someone.
